guideTitle: The Best Office Chairs Under $500 for Real Adjustment
metaTitle: Best Office Chairs Under $500: Ergonomic and Executive Picks (2026)
metaDescription: We compared office chairs under $500 on seat depth, lumbar and arm adjustment, weight capacity and warranty, from SIHOO and Branch to Steelcase, HON and Serta.
introParagraphs: Between $300 and $500, the question changes from whether a chair adjusts to how much, and how long the warranty lasts. Seat depth, 4D armrests and adjustable or self-adjusting lumbar are common at this price; what varies is the warranty, the brand behind it and whether the chair is built for adjustment or for looks.

The eight chairs here fall into three groups: feature-heavy mesh chairs from ELABEST and SIHOO, design-led and commercial chairs from Branch, Steelcase and HON, and two traditional executive chairs from SUNNOW and Serta that trade adjustment for padding and styling.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, adjustment ranges, weight ratings, warranty terms and price position, not hands-on testing.

elabest-x100-premium.summary: Seat depth, 4D arms, dynamic lumbar and a five-year warranty for about $350.
elabest-x100-premium.description:
The ELABEST X100 is the most complete package for the money here: a suspended mesh back, dynamic lumbar support, 4D armrests, seat depth adjustment and a five-year warranty for about $350 at the time of writing.

That list matches or exceeds the adjustment on chairs costing $150 more, and the five-year warranty is longer than the SIHOO B300 Pro's three. The 17- to 21-inch seat range suits many people at a standard desk.

ELABEST is a less established brand than Steelcase, HON or Branch, so if long-term service and brand track record matter to you, the Steelcase Series 1 is the more conservative choice.
pros: Full adjustment including seat depth and 4D arms
elabest-x100-premium.bestFor: Buyers who want the most adjustment and a solid warranty without spending the full $500.
elabest-x100-premium.skipIf: Brand track record and a long warranty matter most; the Steelcase Series 1 offers 12 years.

sihoo-b300-pro-dynamic.summary: SIHOO's flagship with a lumbar that SIHOO says follows you through recline.
sihoo-b300-pro-dynamic.description:
The SIHOO B300 Pro is the pick if lumbar that moves with you is the priority: SIHOO describes a full-motion dynamic lumbar system that adjusts contact across recline angles.

It also has seat depth adjustment and 4D armrests, and at about $330 at the time of writing it is the lowest-priced chair here. On paper it overlaps closely with the ELABEST X100.

The warranty is three years, shorter than the ELABEST's five, which is the main reason to spend $20 more on the ELABEST.
pros: Dynamic lumbar through recline, per SIHOO
sihoo-b300-pro-dynamic.bestFor: Buyers who recline often and want lumbar support that follows them.
sihoo-b300-pro-dynamic.skipIf: Warranty length matters; the ELABEST X100 has similar adjustment and five years.

steelcase-series1-under500.summary: Steelcase's entry chair, with LiveBack and a 12-year warranty at the $500 ceiling.
steelcase-series1-under500.description:
The Steelcase Series 1 is the conservative choice here: an entry-level chair from an established commercial brand with a 12-year warranty, far longer than anything else under $500.

Steelcase lists its LiveBack flexible back, BIFMA certification and a 15.5- to 20.5-inch seat range, which suits shorter users better than most chairs here. Arm options vary by configuration.

It costs about $500 at the time of writing, and it does not list the 4D arms or dynamic lumbar that the ELABEST and SIHOO offer for less. You are paying for the warranty and the brand.
pros: Low seat range suits shorter users
cons: At the top of the budget
Less listed adjustment than cheaper chairs
20.5-inch maximum may be low for tall users
steelcase-series1-under500.bestFor: Buyers who value a long warranty and an established brand over a longer feature list.
steelcase-series1-under500.skipIf: You are tall; the 20.5-inch maximum seat height is on the low side.

hon-sadie-big-tall.summary: A 350 lb rating and an extra-wide seat from HON's commercial range.
hon-sadie-big-tall.description:
The HON Sadie Big and Tall is the choice for larger users: HON lists a 350 lb capacity, an extra-wide seat and BIFMA certification.

The mesh back and 16.5- to 21-inch seat range cover the basics. The listing does not describe seat depth or 4D arm adjustment, so it offers less adjustment than the ELABEST or SIHOO.

If you do not need the extra capacity and width, the mesh chairs here give you more adjustment for less.
cons: Less listed adjustment than the mesh chairs
hon-sadie-big-tall.bestFor: Larger users who need a wider seat and a 350 lb rating.
hon-sadie-big-tall.skipIf: You are of average build; the ELABEST X100 offers more adjustment for less.

branch-pro-minimalist.summary: Branch's full-adjustment chair with a clean home-office look and a five-year warranty.
branch-pro-minimalist.description:
The Branch Pro is for buyers who want a chair that looks at home in a living space as well as a workspace, with full adjustment underneath.

It lists 4D armrests, adjustable lumbar, seat depth adjustment and a five-year warranty. The 16- to 20.5-inch seat range suits shorter to average-height users.

At about $500 at the time of writing it costs more than the ELABEST X100, which lists similar adjustment. You are paying mostly for the design.
cons: At the top of the budget
Low maximum seat height for tall users
branch-pro-minimalist.bestFor: Home offices where appearance matters as much as adjustment.
branch-pro-minimalist.skipIf: Looks are secondary; the ELABEST X100 offers similar adjustment for less.

branch-classic-value.summary: Branch's styling for about $140 less than the Pro, with 2D arms.
branch-classic-value.description:
The Branch Classic keeps Branch's design at about $140 less than the Pro at the time of writing, with fewer adjustments.

The arms are 2D rather than 4D, and the listing mentions adjustable lumbar and tilt tension but not seat depth. It keeps the five-year warranty.

At this price it competes directly with the ELABEST X100, which lists more adjustment. Choose the Classic for its look and the Branch warranty.
pros: Branch styling at a lower price
branch-classic-value.bestFor: Buyers who like Branch's design and do not need 4D arms or seat depth adjustment.
branch-classic-value.skipIf: You want seat depth adjustment; the ELABEST X100 or Branch Pro list it.

sunnow-leather-footrest.summary: A PU leather executive chair with a footrest and 90–140° recline.
sunnow-leather-footrest.description:
The SUNNOW is the only chair here with a footrest, which makes it the pick for anyone who wants to lean back and put their feet up between tasks.

It reclines from 90 to 140 degrees, has an 18- to 22-inch seat range (the highest here) and a 300 lb rating. The upholstery is PU leather rather than genuine leather.

It is built around reclining rather than adjustment: the listing does not mention seat depth, adjustable lumbar or adjustable arms.
sunnow-leather-footrest.bestFor: People who want to alternate between upright work and reclined breaks.
sunnow-leather-footrest.skipIf: You want an adjustable task chair; the mesh chairs here are the better fit.

serta-jackson-executive.summary: Serta's layered foam in a bonded leather executive chair.
serta-jackson-executive.description:
The Serta Jackson is the traditional executive option: a high-back bonded leather chair with Serta's SmartLayers foam, which Serta describes as borrowing from its mattress designs.

It lists padded arms, a tilt lock, a 300 lb rating and a 17.5- to 21.5-inch seat range. It suits buyers who want padding and a classic look more than adjustment.

Bonded leather tends to show surface wear sooner than genuine leather, and the chair lists no lumbar, arm or seat depth adjustment.
serta-jackson-executive.bestFor: Buyers who want a padded, traditional executive chair.
serta-jackson-executive.skipIf: Adjustment matters more than style; any of the mesh chairs here offer more.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Seat depth adjustment lets the seat support more of your thigh without pushing you off the backrest. The ELABEST, SIHOO and Branch Pro list it; most of the others do not.
Ranges here start as low as 15.5 inches (Steelcase Series 1) and reach 22 inches (SUNNOW). Shorter users should check the minimum, taller users the maximum.
This is where the price differences show most. Warranties here run from three years (SIHOO) to five (ELABEST, Branch) and 12 (Steelcase).
Only some listings state a capacity. The HON Sadie lists 350 lb; the SUNNOW and Serta list 300 lb. We would choose a chair rated comfortably above your weight.
4D arms move up and down, forward and back, in and out, and pivot. 2D arms, like the Branch Classic's, do less. Check the listing rather than the word "adjustable".

faq.q: Is $500 enough for a good office chair?
faq.a: For many buyers, yes. In this guide, chairs from about $330 list seat depth adjustment, 4D arms and dynamic lumbar. Spending more typically buys longer warranties, more refined mechanisms and brand service rather than new basic adjustments.

faq.q: Which chair here is best for lower-back support?
faq.a: Look for adjustable or dynamic lumbar plus seat depth adjustment. The ELABEST X100 and SIHOO B300 Pro list both. If you have a back condition, a clinician's advice is more useful than any chair listing; see our [office chair for back pain](/guide/best-office-chair-for-back-pain) guide for chairs selected around lumbar and seat-depth adjustment.

faq.q: How does a chair under $500 compare to a high-end chair?
faq.a: The basic adjustments are often similar. The differences tend to be warranty length, materials, the refinement of the mechanism and the service behind the brand. The Steelcase Series 1 is the closest to that end of the market here, largely because of its 12-year warranty.

faq.q: Should I buy a gaming chair or an office chair under $500?
faq.a: For upright desk work, a mesh office chair with seat depth and lumbar adjustment is usually the better fit. If you prefer to recline, a chair built around recline, like the SUNNOW with its footrest, may suit you better.

bottomLine: For most buyers, the ELABEST X100 is the place to start: seat depth, 4D arms, dynamic lumbar and a five-year warranty for well under $500. The SIHOO B300 Pro is similar for a little less with a shorter warranty, and the Steelcase Series 1 trades features for a 12-year warranty and an established brand.

The HON Sadie is the choice for larger users, the Branch chairs for anyone who prioritizes design, and the SUNNOW and Serta Jackson for buyers who want a reclining or traditional executive chair and can accept less adjustment.
